title: He goes before you (Mark 16:7)
hookLine: the angel's words: he goes ahead of you, you'll see him there
tomorrow: what can you see from the top that you missed on the climb?
last: THE LORD BLESS YOU AND KEEP YOU.

cards: A first day, a move, a goodbye: excited and terrified about the same thing, and the two feelings refuse to take turns. Mark's Easter morning holds both.
At sunrise, Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome walk to a tomb with spices, worrying out loud: "Who shall roll us away the stone from the door of the sepulchre?"
They arrive, and the stone is already rolled back. The problem they carried up the road has been handled before they got there.

teach.b: Inside sits a young man in a white garment. "Be not affrighted," he says. "He is risen; he is not here."
Then a message: "But go your way, tell his disciples and Peter that he goeth before you into Galilee: there shall ye see him, as he said unto you." Look at three pieces. And Peter.
Days before, Peter had denied knowing Jesus; the message names him on his own.
Goeth before you: not waiting for them to catch up, already on the road ahead.

As he said unto you: on the night of his arrest Jesus had quoted the prophet, "I will smite the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered," and in the same breath, "after that I am risen, I will go before you into Galilee."
The promise was made knowing they'd scatter.
Then Mark adds something honest: the women flee, trembling, "for they were afraid." Fear and good news on the same morning, in the same people.
Christians hear Easter hope in this line: the road ahead isn't empty; someone has gone on in front.
And notice where he goes. Galilee, where it all began, by the lake with the nets. The road forward runs through ordinary places, with him already there.

how: Churches read Mark's account of the empty tomb among the Easter readings, and some Christians greet one another at Easter with 'He is risen,' a line from this same scene.

games.q: what does “he goes before you” mean?
o: walking behind you to keep watch on you
already on the road ahead, waiting for you
leaving you behind to find your own way

games.q: the empty tomb — tap the pairs.
p: who shall roll us away the stone?
named on his own after denying
I will go before you into Galilee

s: in Mark, the messenger at the tomb is called an angel
Mark says 'a young man… clothed in a long white garment.' Matthew's account has an angel.
the message at the tomb names Peter on his own
'tell his disciples and Peter' (Mark 16:7), days after he denied knowing Jesus.
Mark says the women left the tomb calm and full of joy
they fled, trembling, 'for they were afraid' (Mark 16:8).

games.q: your cousin let down his whole team and is sure he's "out" for good. what detail in Mark 16:7 speaks to that?
o: the stone: problems simply roll away by themselves.
'and Peter': the one who denied him, named on his own.
the spices: keep doing your duty and don't think about it.
games.why: Peter had denied knowing Jesus (Mark 14:66–72). the first message from the empty tomb singles him out by name: and Peter.

practice: Stand or sit facing the door you'll walk out of next.

Let one thing ahead of you come to mind, tomorrow, next week, a hope you haven't said out loud, and hold it there in front of you, without flinching, the way a road looks when someone has gone on ahead.

wordCard.voice: He goes before you. The message at the empty tomb: already on the road, ahead of the disciples and Peter, waiting in Galilee.

orig.note: Greek: he goes ahead, he leads the way. the verb behind 'he goeth before you' in Mark 16:7.

carryVoice: Keep this: he goes before you, a promise made on the night they all scattered. That's day seventeen-ninety.
